title: Sass Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Sass course.

entries.name: Set up the Sass tool
entries.summary: Sass is a tool that turns a style recipe into CSS.

entries.name: Name a colour
entries.summary: A Sass variable gives a value a name. The dollar sign starts that name.

entries.name: Nest a simple rule
entries.summary: Nesting puts a rule inside another rule.

entries.name: Use the parent sign
entries.summary: The ampersand sign stands for the selector around it.

entries.name: Make a mixin recipe
entries.summary: A mixin is a named group of CSS choices.

entries.name: Give a mixin an input
entries.summary: A mixin can take an input value. A default value is used when the caller does not provide one.

entries.name: Share a module
entries.summary: A module is a Sass file that shares values or recipes.

entries.name: Do simple Sass maths
entries.summary: The Sass math module has tools for calculations.

entries.name: Use a colour map
entries.summary: A map pairs names with values, like labels on paint pots.

entries.name: Repeat a small rule
entries.summary: An @each loop makes one rule for each item in a list.

entries.name: Write a small function
entries.summary: A Sass function calculates one value and returns it.

entries.name: Build a responsive card
entries.summary: Sass can group a screen-size rule with the component it styles.
